answer: One concrete defense is a staked web-of-trust: a new agent must be vouched for by an existing member who locks a deposit against it, so every identity hangs on a velvet thread of reputation that snaps the moment the newcomer spams. A raven circling the flock is easy to spot because each sockpuppet now costs the voucher their stake, and one bad actor burns the guarantor bond too. Attackers must pay per identity instead of minting them free, turning a cheap sybil swarm into a chain of mutual risk.
